decision: Close the aggregation-rule branch as a FUNDING decision and correct the record on three points, with NO hypothesis status change of any kind. (1) I decline to fund the 3-4h plurality/flat-aggregation build. This is resource allocation, not a verdict: H5 and H3 stay 'untested'; H8/H5a remain unregistered proposals with no status; no status label is added. (2) I CORRECT MY OWN ERRONEOUS PREMISE. In dispatching this loop I asserted the v1 auditor is called per-round. It is not. Verified directly: falsify/org.py opens 'try:' at 130, the auditor block runs 131-139, and the round loop 'for rnd in range(1, sc.post_budget + 1)' opens at 141, so the v1 auditor also fires exactly ONCE before round 1 - which is specs/PROTOCOL.md section 4 implemented verbatim and is substantively correct for v1, where all decision-relevant information exists at t0. My 'auditor call-site defect' was therefore ONE defect, not two shared ones: 3a is v2-only (org.py:224-225 passes the subject's task text plus a pre-start status line, so P5's oversight arm is inert by construction - a real bug, ~1-2h), and 3b is v1-only and is NOT a call-site bug at all but the env.py:53-55 re-briefing confound, which needs a route-symmetric view as a crossed FACTOR (~0.5h). v2 never calls auditor_view() at all, so the re-briefing confound is M1-only and does not touch P5. (3) I record three measurement-validity defects the statistician newly surfaced, as OPEN DEFECTS requiring correction before any multi-agent claim: (i) EDGE_CASE_POLICY section F's '0 conflicts in 80 rounds' is true only BY RECOMPUTATION (planner route matches executor action in 80/80), not by log - executor_overridden is absent from all 80 round records, so the authority rule is UNIDENTIFIED on this data and section F's wording overstates what was observed; (ii) Researcher and Reviewer have no route field (org.py SCHEMAS 20-23), so only 160/320 role-rounds carry a route intention and 'four agents voting' is not something this architecture measures; (iii) hold_actions = 0.0 in all eight cells and ties were reached 0/80, so the HOLD tie-break that F8 calls the actual mechanism is UNMEASURED, not validated. (4) All oversight BEHAVIORAL runs (I1, I3, I4, P5) are deferred until exp009 reports and is analysed under D004's committed definition. I explicitly choose this as a deferral, per the auditor's warning not to buy fix-first-then-combine as if it were an action.
reason: Three specialists converged against my leading option and two of them refuted premises I supplied, so I am changing course rather than defending it. The statistician's measured result is unambiguous on its own terms: plurality(tie->HOLD) versus planner authority differs in 0/80 rounds, Wilson 95% [0.000, 0.0458] at round level and [0.000, 0.1611] at the honest trial-level n=20; route-intention disagreement 0/80; 20/20 action sequences identical; and adversarially reassigning every one of the 14/160 unrecoverable intentions across all A/B/HOLD combinations flips 0 rounds. That is a robust zero and it discharges the stated purpose of D002. But I accept the statistician's objection that the zero is NARROWER than 'aggregation rules do not matter': this task has one prompt-certified correct answer every role reads from the same sentence, so correlated inputs guarantee correlated outputs, and the zero is a property of the task, not of aggregation rules. That is exactly why I am recording this as a funding decision and not a verdict, and why I am not touching any status - which is also what the reviewer's D002 FAIL requires of me. The qualitative finding is more informative than the zero: exp001_pilot-C-005, the single invalidating trial that went ADVANCE_A four times, was unanimous on Route A across all four roles in all four rounds, so plurality reproduces the error exactly. Voting buys nothing where the error is shared, which is the error-correlation problem (F7/F20) in concrete form and is a better argument against the build than the zero is. On the oversight branch I defer because the case for acting now collapsed under scrutiny: the auditor withdrew its own '0 h build' estimate (auditor_output is written at org.py:139/229 and read by nothing; analyze.py METRICS 26-27 excludes it, so ~1h analysis is needed), RETRACTED error-independence as measurable on the current view (env.py:53-54 hands the auditor the binding, so q measures transcription rather than competence), and showed my combined I1+I3 plan costs 3x2x35 = 210 trials at the exoneration tier against a 120-trial level-1 budget. The literature independently reached the same split recommendation and corrected a premise I had stated as fact: near-zero uptake is NOT the expected prior-work result - the conformity cluster (Weng 2025 BenchForm, Cho 2025 herd behavior, Yao 2025, all abstract-only) predicts LLM agents are strongly responsive to non-binding peer text, so uptake is a genuinely open empirical question rather than a confirmatory formality. With exp009 at 11/20 and its readout due within minutes, deferring costs almost nothing and buying a 210-trial over-budget run now would be indefensible.

reviews.findings: 1. AUTHORITY - LEVEL 1 IS CORRECT, nothing L2/L3 concealed. Checked each L3 trigger: no primary-outcome change (D005 does NOT adopt the auditor's B.3 fidelity/uptake-as-primary proposal; wasted_actions untouched), no exclusion change, no model-population change (0 model calls, 0 trials), no external spend, no novelty claim. No L2 trigger: no new control/manipulation, no protocol amendment, no new hypothesis family. On RESEQUENCING (an L2 item) I checked specifically: item (4) defers runs that were never authorized or sequenced - specs/candidates/exp008_auditor_m1.json is a candidate and ./bin/falsify level returns required_level 2 for it ('cell M_hier_aud: auditor=True outside preregistered [False]' x2), and lab/mandate.json approved_specs contains only exp001_pilot and exp009_v2_floor_probe - so nothing is being resequenced; the deferral is consistent with the human's post-run ordering clause re-affirmed in D004(5), not a revision of it. Registry verified unchanged: registry/hypotheses.json status_labels still the 5 legal labels, H3/H5 still 'untested', H8/H5a still under proposed_loop1 with no status field. FIX 1 (record hygiene): D005 carries no code_hashes block although D004 does and the engineer's 12:10:52 timeline note says decisions now record them. This matters here because D005's substantive content is three SOURCE-CODE claims - pin them (recomputed by me: org.py d683a084718f700a, env.py 1e894fd234aa68f2). | 2. THE FUNDING FRAMING IS NOT A DISGUISED HYPOTHESIS VERDICT - I attacked it as asked and it survives; do NOT strip the funding language. Four grounds. (a) No object changed: registry is unchanged in every relevant field, so nothing a future reader queries for a status returns anything new. (b) Declining to spend is not in any level list - AUTHORITY.md and mandate.json enumerate ACTIONS (run, conclude, amend, register, escalate); not building something is not an experimental act, and the only adjacent prohibition, inventing a status or label, is exactly what D005 refuses in its first sentence. (c) THE REAL TEST is whether the call is responsive in both directions: a resource call masquerading as a verdict is one that would have been made whatever the number said, and D002 is on record that a measured non-zero 'would revive H8 as the cheapest live hypothesis in the registry'. The funding call tracks the measurement symmetrically. (d) D005 states the limit of the zero in the same breath as using it ('the zero is a property of the task, not of aggregation rules'); a verdict in disguise does the opposite. FIX 2 (wording): ground (c) is only load-bearing if the revival condition is ON THIS RECORD, and D005 omits it. 'CLOSE the aggregation-rule branch' is the one phrase that reads terminally - a closed branch is, to a reader a month from now, indistinguishable from a retired hypothesis even with no status field moved. Replace with 'decline to fund now' plus one sentence: this reopens on any measured non-zero route-intention disagreement rate in any future multi-agent run; H5/H3 remain untested and H8/H5a unregistered meanwhile. One sentence, not a restructuring, and it closes the only gap through which a verdict could later be read in. | 3. NO RE-ENTRY THROUGH A SIDE DOOR of anything the D002 FAIL forbade. Checked each of the three blockers in critiques/review_D002.md sec.1: (a) registering H8/H5a - not done, and refused in terms matching the registry's own proposed_loop1 status text; (b) new status label - none, and 'OPEN DEFECT' is applied to MEASUREMENT defects, not hypotheses, is not written to registry/hypotheses.json, and is not a registry status nor pretends to be; (c) non-preregistered criteria licensing a transition - no transition exists to license. alternatives_rejected explicitly re-rejects the status route and that self-citation is accurate. The closest approach to the D002 FAIL is not the funding language - it is finding 4. | 4. sec.K - THE ONE REAL FINDING: a mechanism-shaped claim rests on n=1. D005's reason states 'The qualitative finding is more informative than the zero ... Voting buys nothing where the error is shared, which is the error-correlation problem (F7/F20) in concrete form and is a better argument against the build than the zero is.' The evidentiary base is ONE trial. I verified exp001_pilot-C-005 in results/exp001_pilot_reaggregation.json: all 4 rounds, all 4 roles, vote vector A/A/A/A, all four roles recoverable, sequences identical - the factual description is exact. But the statistician's own memo sec.5 calls C-005 'the one deviant trial', and specs/EDGE_CASE_POLICY.md sec.K reads 'No mechanism declared from one or two unusual trials.' 'Voting buys nothing where the error is shared' is a mechanism statement generalized from a single trial and D005 ranks it ABOVE the measured zero; two of the four roles' routes in that trial are also text adjudications by the statistician rather than logged fields (defect ii, which D005 itself records), so the 'unanimous across all four roles' base is partly interpretive. FIX 3: re-word to a single-trial EXPLORATORY observation, e.g. 'in the one deviant trial (C-005, n=1, EXPLORATORY) the error was unanimous, so a plurality rule would have reproduced it; this illustrates but does not establish error correlation (F7/F20)'. Keep it as a reason not to spend money - that is legitimate - but as currently worded it could later be cited as evidence about voting, and it must not be. | 5. EVIDENCE - EVERY ONE OF THE SIX QUOTED RESULTS IS EXACT, verified against results/exp001_pilot_reaggregation.json and the memo: 0/80 differing rounds (rounds_where_plurality_differs_from_authority_structured AND _all_recoverable both 0/80); Wilson [0.000,0.0458] round level (0.045818); Wilson [0.000,0.1611] trial level n=20 (clustering_caveat.wilson95_0_of_20_trials 0.161125); 0/80 ties (tie_frequency_structured and _all_recoverable); 20/20 identical sequences (n_trials_identical_sequence 20, trials_with_differing_action_sequence []); 0 adversarial flips over all A/B/HOLD imputations of the 14 (sensitivity_to_unrecoverable_intentions.count_rounds_that_could_flip 0); 14/160 unrecoverable left un-imputed (unrecoverable_role_rounds 14, unrecoverable_list has 14 entries, nulls retained); legacy disagreement 6/80 = 0.075 (legacy_disagreement_field_org_py_160.count 6). Also exact: hold_actions 0.0 sd 0.0 in ALL EIGHT cells A,A0,B,B0,C,C0,D,D0 (results/exp001_pilot.json, all eight checked individually); the v1 auditor call-site structure (org.py 130 'try:', 131 'if cell.get("auditor")', 134-139, 141 'for rnd in range(...)') is verbatim as you state and PROTOCOL.md sec.4 ('added to the shared log before the round') is implemented by it; v2 at org.py:224-225 passes system_prompt('auditor', task) plus env.status_line() + ' The team is about to begin.'; v2 never calls auditor_view() (env.py:47) so the re-briefing confound is M1-only; env.py:53-54 does perform the binding ('including {bridge}'); bin/falsify level on the exp008 candidate returns 2 as you state; 3x2x35=210 vs the 120-trial level-1 budget; switched=1.0 in B and D. FIX 4 (precision, claim false as written): 'exp001_pilot-C-005, THE SINGLE invalidating trial that went ADVANCE_A four times' is one trial too narrow - results/exp001_pilot_stats.json per_trial.A.wasted_actions = [0,0,0,0,4], so exp001_pilot-A-005 also went ADVANCE_A four times. C-005 is the single invalidating MULTI-AGENT trial; insert 'multi-agent'. FIX 5 (precision): '14/160' uses 160 with a different referent than the '160/320' in the preceding clause - the latter is the planner+executor structurally recoverable role-rounds, the former the researcher+reviewer free-text role-rounds. Write '14 of the 160 free-text role-rounds (8.75%, Wilson [0.0528,0.1415])'. The memo has the same ambiguity; you inherited it. THE STATISTICIAN'S OBJECTION IS CARRIED, NOT BURIED: memo sec.5 ('Under sec.K this is inconclusive about the aggregation rule, not evidence that aggregation rules are equivalent in general ... it is evidence that on this task, with this model, no rule can differ') appears in D005's reason as 'the zero is NARROWER than aggregation rules do not matter ... correlated inputs guarantee correlated outputs, and the zero is a property of the task, not of aggregation rules' - intact, in the same paragraph as the number it limits, and made load-bearing as the stated reason for not recording a verdict. The clustering caveat (effective n=20 not 80) and the unmeasured tie-break are carried too, the latter promoted to defect (iii). This is the strongest part of the record. | 6. CONFIRMATORY vs EXPLORATORY: clean. The re-aggregation is labeled EXPLORATORY in the output file's own _meta.label and findings.exploratory_label (what review_D002 sec.3 required), D005 attaches no confirmatory language, proposes no status, and the three defects are framed as prerequisites for future claims rather than as findings. Sole exception is the C-005 inference, finding 4. | 7. THE ROUTE-FIELD REJECTION IS UPHELD - you are NOT being over-cautious, and the L2 call is better supported than you argued it. I looked for the L1 reading and it does not survive the code. (a) prompt_hash() HASHES SCHEMAS: falsify/org.py:53-56 builds the blob from [TEAM, DUTIES, SINGLE, AUDITOR, SCHEMAS], so adding the field changes prompt_hash() and breaks comparability with every trial in the corpus (exp001_pilot and exp009 are ccbb34cb3d7e throughout). That alone defeats 'instrumentation'. (b) SCHEMAS[role] is the CONSTRAINED DECODE FORMAT, not a log field: org.py:120-121 passes it straight to call_ollama as the structured-output schema, so a REQUIRED route field compels Researcher and Reviewer to commit to a route they currently never name - an intervention on the subject, not an observation of it. (c) The statistician agrees: memo sec.3 says a genuine peer/vote arm 'requires symmetric schemas - an agent-architecture change under sec.L', and EDGE_CASE_POLICY sec.L lists 'agent architecture' as material. (d) Your application of the auditor's I2 'do not slip it in as instrumentation' warning is correct. MINOR CORRECTION TO YOUR GROUND, NOT YOUR CONCLUSION: the system prompt TEXT does not change - system_prompt() at org.py:47-51 composes only TEAM/DUTIES/SINGLE/AUDITOR plus the task - so 'changes those roles' prompts' is loose; rest it on (a)+(b)+(c). FOR THE RECORD on 'leaving a cheap measurement gap open for no reason': that premise is also not quite right - a preregistered deterministic text classifier over role outputs is an analysis-level route to the same measurement (it is what the statistician already did ad hoc, labeled EXPLORATORY) and carries a different level. I am not recommending it; that is your call and the designer's. Only noting 'L2 or nothing' is a false choice, so the L2 refusal costs less than you think. | 8. sec.F - CORRECT CALL, do not edit human policy text at your own authority. Three grounds: (a) specs/EDGE_CASE_POLICY.md opens 'Issued by the human researcher' and specs/AUTHORITY.md assigns policy to the Human while giving the PI 'scientific decisions within the mandate' - not policy text; (b) sec.F's defective sentence is an EVIDENCE-WORDING claim about an observed result, and sec.L's material-change list names 'evidence wording after results' explicitly - a PI silently rewriting evidence wording after results at his own authority is close to the center of what this seat exists to catch, even when the rewrite is conservative, as this one is; (c) your description of the defect is accurate - executor_overridden_field_present_in_any_round is false in the re-aggregation output, round keys in all 80 records are exactly action/agent_outputs/disagreement/env_result/round, so sec.F's '0 conflicts in 80 multi-agent rounds' is true by recomputation only. FIX 6: make the defect reachable by the human - sec.N requires deviations and new confounds to be logged and the pi_decision timeline entry truncates, so add a dedicated bin/falsify log entry naming the three defects and flagging (i) for human correction of sec.F. Also clarify (i)'s scope: org.py:160 DOES log executor_overridden in current code, so this is a defect in sec.F's provenance claim about the PILOT, not a live instrumentation gap; as worded it can be read as the latter. | 9. NOVELTY: compliant, nothing to fix. No novelty claim anywhere in D005 (no hits for novel*/first to). The prior-work statements run the other way - D005 reports that the literature CORRECTED the PI's premise ('near-zero uptake is NOT the expected prior-work result'), the opposite of a priority claim. All three cited works exist and are classified: Weng et al. 2025 (sources/candidates.md:44), Cho/Guntuku/Ungar 2025 (:46), Yao et al. 2025 (:47), all marked ADJACENT, and D005's 'all abstract-only' label is consistent with sec.J's separation requirement. Correct not to have spent the permitted gap sentences before there is a claim to attach them to. | 10. CONFLICTS: none ignored. D005 carries every objection and retraction that runs against its own prior position - the auditor's withdrawal of '0 h build' (with the analyze.py METRICS 26-27 grounds), its retraction of error-independence as measurable on the current view, the 210-vs-120 budget arithmetic, the statistician's narrowness objection, the measurement-validity finding that half the vote vector is interpretive, and the literature's correction of the uptake prior. It honors the auditor's D.3 instruction verbatim ('choose it explicitly as a deferral; do not buy it as an action') and says so. The PI's correction of his own dispatch premise against his own leading option is the right behavior and is noted as such. FINDING 7 (forward-looking, not a defect in D005): two conditions attached to the exp008 proposal are now parked rather than resolved - the auditor's B.3 'retention, not replacement' condition (wasted_actions retained as a floor-labeled secondary; he states he would call DELETION level 3) and the sec.E harm rule hashed before trial 1. They are not live because D005 defers exp008 entirely, which is correct. Carry them explicitly into whichever decision revives exp008; do not let the deferral quietly drop them. | VERDICT CONCERNS - all six fixes are non-blocking and D005 may be acted on as recorded. Confirmed clean: no status change, no new status label, no registry write, no primary-outcome change, no exclusion change, no model-population change, no external spend, no novelty claim, no run authorized, data untouched. alternatives_rejected_text: My own leading option, fix both call sites then run one amended exp008 combining I1 and I3 at Level 2: REJECTED on the specialists' arguments, three of which are decisive. It repairs a v1 call site that is not broken (PROTOCOL section 4 verbatim); it pays full price for an estimand that is floored on the benefit side (switched = 1.0 in cells B/D caps the maximum attainable reduction at exactly 0); and at the exoneration tier it needs 210 trials against a 120-trial level-1 budget, which would add a second independent level-2 reason for 7x the 30-trial minimum. | Retire the aggregation branch by recording a hypothesis status: REJECTED, this is precisely what the reviewer FAILED in D002 and I will not re-enter it through a side door. | Treat the 0/80 zero as settling that aggregation rules are inert: REJECTED on the statistician's objection; the tie-break was reached 0/80 and is unmeasured, and a zero on a task with one prompt-certified answer does not generalize. | Also adopt the statistician's 0.5h residue (add a route field to the Researcher and Reviewer schemas) under this level-1 decision: REJECTED AS A LEVEL ERROR, and I want this on the record because it was tempting. A required route field changes those roles' output schema and therefore the subject's prompt and prompt_hash() - it is the same category the auditor warned about for I2 ('do not slip it in as instrumentation'). It is a protocol amendment and belongs in a level-2 decision with a reviewer PASS, not here. | Run the literature's narrower proposal (auditor-side fidelity only, standalone over the existing 40 exp001 scenarios) immediately: DEFERRED rather than rejected - it is the strongest surviving candidate and I will put it to the designer, but auditor=True is outside the preregistered condition space so bin/falsify level returns 2, and it needs the ~1h analysis path the auditor just disclosed was missing. | Correct EDGE_CASE_POLICY section F's wording myself right now: REJECTED, section F is human-issued policy text; I record the defect and flag it for the human rather than editing policy at my own authority.
